In Assam, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal will flag off the maiden international cargo voyage from the newly constructed Bogibeel Terminal in Dibrugarh today.  Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma will also join the flag-off ceremony.Akashvani correspondent reports that with the flagging off of the cargo voyage, Dibrugarh is set to restore its pre-Independence legacy as a major inland waterway trade hub.For the first time in more than eight decades, an international cargo consignment will sail directly from Assam to a foreign port. Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal will flag off the cargo voyage at 11 a.m. today.The inaugural shipment consists of 1,080 tonnes of methanol produced by Assam Petro-Chemicals Limited at Namrup. Two renovated cargo vessels will transport the consignment to Pangaon Port in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 are set to conclude today, bringing more than two weeks of exciting sporting action to an end. India has put up an impressive performance at the 20th Asian Games, securing fourth place in the overall medal standings with a tally of 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.The closing ceremony of the games will be held at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya, Japan. The event is scheduled to begin at 2:30 PM IST. India’s women’s flag-bearer for the closing ceremony has been confirmed as shooting star Neeru Dhanda, who will proudly carry the Tricolour in Nagoya. The ceremony will feature traditional closing proceedings, including the parade of athletes and the formal handover to the Doha 2030 organising committee.

. India’s registered manufacturing sector recorded strong growth in financial year 2025 (FY25), with industrial output rising 7.81 per cent and total employment increasing almost 7.2 per cent over the previous year.According to the Annual Survey of Industries data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation today, the total number of establishments in this sector increased from 2.60 lakh in FY24 to 2.67 lakh in FY25, representing a growth of 2.64 per cent. The highest number of establishments was reported in Tamil Nadu, followed by Gujarat and Maharashtra.Meanwhile, total emoluments paid to the workforce also increased by over 12 per cent in 2024-25 on an annual basis. Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana have emerged as the top 5 states in employment, having a share of more than 56 per cent of the total manufacturing employment of the country in FY25.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said that India’s economic strength and resilience have been built over the past decade through a combination of fiscal prudence, infrastructure investment, banking reforms, improved delivery mechanisms and consistent reforms.Addressing the 5th Kautilya economic conclave in New Delhi, the Finance Minister said that the government has advanced the national frameworks through GST, insolvency and bankruptcy code and the four labour codes. She said that India had navigated the shocks of the past four years with its fundamentals intact, citing 7.8 percent real GDP growth in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27.The Finance Minister said that the IMF projects India’s general government debt to decline from 83.4 percent of GDP in 2026 to 77.7 percent in 2031 against a rising global trend.On infrastructure development, Ms Sitharaman said, capital expenditure for this fiscal had been budgeted at 12.22 lakh crore rupees. She added that the national highway network had expanded by about 61 per cent and the number of operational airports had more than doubled since 2014.She also highlighted that more than 52 crore collateral-free loans have been sanctioned under PM MUDRA Yojana. Highlighting the PM Awas Yojana, PM Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, Ms Sitaharaman said that these initiatives have strengthened citizens’ capacity to participate in growth and build capacities to fight the challenges.

. India and Canada will kick off the fifth round of negotiations for their proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) in Ottawa from tomorrow, as both sides aim to conclude the trade pact by the end of 2026. The five-day round, led by the chief negotiators of the two countries, will continue till 9th of October. The previous round concluded in New Delhi on 18th of September, with officials now pushing for faster progress towards a final agreement.In March this year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Canadian counterpart Mark Carney set a year-end target to complete the negotiations for the CEPA between the two countries and agreed to deepen bilateral collaboration in the energy and critical mineral sectors during their meeting in New Delhi. According to the joint statement issued after their summit, the leaders expressed confidence that a comprehensive trade framework would serve as a durable economic anchor for the partnership and support the shared aspiration of expanding bilateral trade to 4.65 lakh crore Rs by 2030.India-Canada bilateral trade in goods stood at 8.66 billion US dollars in 2024-25, while India’s exports to the country touched 4.22 billion US dollars.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined by 18.3 billion US dollars (USD) to 747.5 billion US dollars during the week ended the 25th of September. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 15.5 billion USD to 615.4 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 2.5 billion USD to 108.7 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 97 million USD to 18.64 billion USD. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped by 86 million to 4.8 billion USD.

. The Asian Games 2026 have officially concluded at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya, bringing more than two weeks of action-packed competition across 43 disciplines to an end. The President of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) officially declared the Games closed, marking the conclusion of a memorable edition of the continental sporting event. The ceremonial torch and flag from the inaugural Asian Games were handed over to representatives of Qatar, which will host the next edition in Doha in 2030. The handover marks the official transition from Nagoya 2026 to Doha 2030. Indian shooter Neeru Dhanda, who won two gold medals and a silver during the Games, carried the Indian flag as the country’s flag-bearer at the closing ceremony. India finished fourth in the overall medal standings, with an impressive 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver, and 37 bronze.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended compliments to every member of the Indian contingent as the Asian Games 2026 draw to a close, for representing the nation with determination, passion and remarkable sporting spirit. In his message, he congratulated all the medal winners whose performances have brought immense joy to the nation. He hoped that these games would inspire even greater achievements in the years ahead and strengthen sports at the grassroots too.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has paid tribute to Rani Durgavati on her birth anniversary today.In a social media post, Mr Singh said that Rani Durgavati accorded the highest priority to the welfare of her subjects and the prosperity of the state, while promoting endeavors for the public good.He added that the reign of Rani Durgavati was inspired by a spirit of benevolence toward the people, farsightedness, and good governance.The Defence Minister emphasised that the courage, sacrifice, and ideals of Rani Durgavati will forever continue to inspire generations to come.

. Swiss President Guy Parmelin will arrive in New Delhi tomorrow for a three-day state visit to India. He will be accompanied by a high-level delegation comprising senior officials and business leaders. Prime Minister Modi and President Parmelin will hold bilateral discussions to review progress in bilateral cooperation across a wide range of areas. These include trade and investment, science, technology and innovation, mobility, culture and people-to-people contact. They will also exchange views on regional and global developments, including cooperation in multilateral fora.Our correspondent reports that this will be President Parmelin’s first State visit to India and second visit during this year. Earlier, in February this year, he visited India to participate in the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi. The visiting dignitary will meet President Droupadi Murmu tomorrow evening. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar will also call on President Parmelin.The visit assumes added significance in view of his participation in the 2nd India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on 7th of October to mark the first anniversary of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement coming into force. Among EFTA countries, Switzerland is the largest trade and investment partner of India. India and Switzerland share longstanding friendly relations. This visit will further strengthen bilateral relations, building upon the regular high-level exchanges and deepen cooperation in new areas of mutual interest.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated wrestler Antim Panghal on winning the silver medal in the Women’s 53 kilogram Freestyle Wrestling event at the Asian Games. In a social media post, Mr Modi wished her continued success, expressing confidence that her achievement would inspire other athletes.The Prime Minister also congratulated the Indian women’s golf team comprising Aditi Ashok, Pranavi Sharath Urs, and Diksha Dagar on clinching the silver medal. Mr Modi commended their determination and passion for the sport, wishing them greater heights in their sports careers.

. Iran has said the Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened until the United States meets seven conditions outlined in a June interim agreement, as Tehran and Washington remain at odds over efforts to end their conflict. Iranian state media today quoted Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf as saying that Tehran’s position on reopening the strategic waterway was completely clear and firm. He said Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened until seven conditions, based on the Islamabad ⁠Memorandum of Understanding are met. Separately, Iranian Army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said Iran would seek to extend the range of its missiles following its recent war with the United States. Speaking to a news agency, he said the conflict had highlighted the need for Iran to develop longer-range missiles and that the country had already begun taking steps in that direction.Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei today said Tehran had conveyed its broad positions on the US response through mediators, while some additional points still needed to be communicated to Washington. Baghaei said, Iran was currently focused on the Strait of Hormuz and that restoring security in the strategically important waterway would require clear and concrete steps from the United States. The June memorandum helped to pave the way for a brief ceasefire between the countries, including provisions relating to the Strait of Hormuz as well as Iran’s nuclear programme.

. The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave will be held from this Saturday in New Delhi, under the theme of ‘Resilience in an Age of Flux’. The Ministry of Finance said that the three-day gathering will bring together more than 180 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries.The Ministry added that the Conclave will feature plenary sessions, interactive parallel sessions and roundtables. The roundtables will focus on issues including attracting foreign direct investment and mobilising domestic capital for long-term investment. The Ministry said that these roundtables will provide opportunities for more focused exchanges among policymakers, economists, investors and practitioners.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will deliver the inaugural address on the first day of the conclave. The conclave will also witness addresses from Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and other Union Ministers. The Ministry informed that the conclave will also feature a special address by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Sanjay Malhotra.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has emphasised that India’s ambition to become Viksit Bharat requires an economy in which enterprises of every size can grow, wherever they begin. She added that the Government has worked to create those conditions over the past 12 years.In an article for a newspaper, the Finance Minister said that GST’s introduction in 2017 established a common national framework for indirect taxation. She highlighted that next-gen GST carries that effort forward, drawing on nine years of implementation and the experience of taxpayers and states.The Finance Minister noted that GST registrations across central and state jurisdictions were about 17.1 million at the end of August, up by nearly 15 per cent from a year earlier.She also said that under the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, next-gen GST was conceived with two connected purposes that were to reduce and rationalise rates and to make compliance easier.She stated that the next phase of process reforms will come before the GST Council shortly and added that these efforts seek to give households relief, businesses greater certainty and taxpayers a system in which they can fulfil their obligations without difficulty.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey asserted that India needs capital markets that can mobilise capital, manage risk and build investor confidence.While addressing the 12th International Convention of the Commodity and Capital Market Participants Association of India in New Delhi today, he said, the regulator is working to strengthen the market structure so that households can invest with confidence, businesses can raise funds for growth, and market intermediaries maintain high standards of conduct. SEBI Chairman said, the regulator is examining concerns related to the settlement price framework for derivatives on expiry days following the introduction of the Closing Auction Session – CAS. The mechanism was introduced to improve price discovery for eligible stocks at market close by using a call-auction process to determine a single equilibrium price instead of relying solely on volume-weighted average prices.He also said, SEBI is working to deepen and improve liquidity in cash markets, expand participation and strengthen securities borrowing and lending. He added that efficient hedging and arbitrage can improve price discovery and strengthen the interaction between cash and derivatives markets. The regulator is also examining position limits for non-agricultural contracts with the aim of improving market liquidity and depth while maintaining risk controls.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. In the Asian Games, Indian archer Neeraj Chauhan upset compatriot Dhiraj Bommadevara 6-4 to bag the bronze medal in the men’s individual recurve event in Nagoya, Japan, today. Neeraj became only the second Indian male after Tarundeep Rai to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. Earlier, top seed Dhiraj went down 3-7 to Paris Olympics bronze medallist Lee Woo Seok in the first semifinal, while Neeraj was outplayed 1-7 by Japanese archer Junya Nakanishi in his last-four stage match. Dhiraj had defeated Uzbekistan’s Amirkhon Sadikov in the quarterfinals, while Neeraj advanced to the semifinals defeating Bhutan’s Lam Dorji.

. The Indian boxing contingent has returned to New Delhi following a triumphant campaign at the 2026 Asian Games. Speaking to the media upon her arrival, boxer Lovlina Borgohain who clinched gold in the Women’s 75 kg category on her birthday shared that the timing made the milestone particularly special. She noted that competing in her second Asian Games gave her the opportunity to upgrade her previous silver medal to gold.While, Boxer Ankush Panghal who also won gold in Men’s 80 kilogram event also expressed his happiness for winning the medal. He said that now he is focusing on the Olympics.Indian boxer Parveen Hooda, who clinched a historic gold medal in the women’s 65 kilogram category has attributed the team’s triumphant campaign to collective hard work and strong institutional backing.   Expressing gratitude, She credited the athletes’ tireless dedication, the strategic guidance of the coaching staff, and the continuous support provided by the Sports Authority of India.

. India concluded its campaign at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings. India’s 2026 Asian Games campaign produced a series of landmark achievements across disciplines.The defining feature of India’s campaign was its clean sweep of gold medals in men’s and women’s cricket, kabaddi and hockey. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games concluded yesterday, bringing more than two weeks of exciting sporting action to an end.In cricket, India retained both titles. The women’s team defeated Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final, while the men’s team overcame Pakistan by 19 runs to complete the golden double.Kabaddi also produced a clean sweep. The women’s team defeated Iran 37-34 to successfully defend its title, while the men came from behind to beat Iran 40-34.Hockey also completed the sweep. The Indian women ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games medal by defeating China 1-0, with Lalremsiami scoring the decisive goal in the 10th minute. It was India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games since 1982.The men’s team defeated Malaysia 5-1 to retain its title and claim India’s fifth men’s hockey gold, following triumphs in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022.It was also the first time India’s men’s and women’s hockey teams won gold at the same Asian Games. Both teams secured qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.Archery was one of India’s most successful disciplines, producing nine medals – five gold, two silver and two bronze. Boxing produced India’s best Asian Games campaign in terms of gold medals, with three gold and three bronze medals.Indian wrestlers won six medals – two gold, two silver and two bronze, making it the country’s best Asian Games wrestling tally since Jakarta 1962.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that the US-India trade deal negotiations are still ongoing and yet to get finalised.Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi today, Mrs Sitharaman said both sides have reached a plateau. She described the agreement under discussion as a hard and rigorously negotiated one.The Minister said the trade balance is very much in India’s favour. Mrs Sitharman said that negotiations used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today emphasised that Russia is a country that stood by India in many ways when India’s security and territorial integrity was under threat. Speaking at the 62nd Munich Security Conference in New Delhi, the External Affairs Minister stressed that at a time when much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to India, Russia was a country with which India’s relations were very good. He said India-Russia relations are shaped by that legacy in many ways. He said the bilateral relationship has widened beyond that today, and it is very much an economic relationship as well. Dr Jaishankar said there are military, nuclear and space components along with a significant amount of trade and investment between the two countries.Dr Jaishankar termed the Russia-Ukraine conflict as unfortunate, saying that India’s position has been very clear that it would like to see an end to this conflict. He expressed New Delhi’s belief that this will require dialogue and diplomacy, and there has to be negotiations in this regard. He admitted that India has, in recent months, become a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. He added that India had conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard, and is trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next 2-3 days. The IMD said thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, Konkan and Goa may experience Hot and Humid weather tomorrow.

. Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) flows turned negative in September after positive flows in July and August. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have offloaded Indian equities worth 35,861 crore rupees last month. Out of the total net outflows, 45,537 crore rupees were withdrawn through sales on stock exchanges, as geopolitical uncertainty, elevated US bond yields, and crude oil prices weighed on investors’ risk appetite. However, the trend of FPI investment through the primary market continued last month, with FPIs infusing 9,676 crore rupees in the primary market in September.Meanwhile, foreign investors also extended their selling to the debt market during the period under review. Last month, outflows from the debt securities through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) stood at 10,431 crore rupees. FPIs withdrew 5,247 crore rupees through General Limit route and 5,049 crore rupees through Voluntary Retention Route (VRR).

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. Indian wrestler Aman Sehrawat clinched the men’s 57kg gold after edging out North Korea’s world champion Chong Song Han 11-7 in a fierce final in Asian Games at Nagoya in Japan today. The 23-year-old Indian, who had won a bronze at the Hangzhou Asian Games, showed immense tactical acumen to thwart a tricky Han and complete his climb to the top of the podium. Aman’s gold also adds to India’s strong showing in wrestling after Sujeet Kalkal won men’s 65kg gold yesterday.

. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi to assess road dust and effectiveness of road cleaning operations across the city.The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has informed that the commission deployed four flying squad teams for the inspection which was carried out yesterday. The Flying Squad Teams inspected 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer ring road which come under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi.The Ministry highlighted that the inspections, which were meant to seek strict implementation of road cleaning and dust mitigation measures, found 17 cases of violation. These violations include accumulation of construction and demolition waste and high visible road dust across inspected road stretches.CAQM has directed PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. It also added the inspection shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures.

. The National Statistics Office (NSO), is conducting the Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions (CAPEX 2026) during the period of October to December 2026.The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation said that the survey is aimed at generating comprehensive and timely information on capital expenditure undertaken and planned by large private corporate sector enterprises. The Ministry added that the survey will provide important inputs for understanding emerging investment trends in the Indian economy.The primary objective of the CAPEX Survey is to collect information on capital expenditure undertaken in the recent financial years , provisional capital expenditure in the current financial year and investment intentions for the forthcoming financial year.The Ministry has appealed all the selected private corporate sector enterprises to extend their full cooperation and participate actively in the CAPEX 2026 Survey.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. Minister of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr Jitendra Singh, will chair the 17th Pension Adalat in New Delhi today.Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions informed that 897 long-pending grievances of super-senior pensioners and family pensioners are to be taken up for redressal.The ministry said Dr Singh will release flyers highlighting the success stories of the 16th Pension Adalat, which was held on 13th May of this year.A booklet containing Frequently Asked Questions on issues concerning family pensioners will also be released during the occasion.The Ministry noted that the Pension Adalats have resolved 20,676 out of a total of 28,797 grievances on the spot across its previous 16 editions, since its inception in 2017, retaining a success rate of 71.79 per cent.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal today.IMD said that conditions are likely to become favourable for further withdrawal of southwest monsoon from most parts of Marathwada and Vidarbha, and some more parts of Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh during the next two days.The Weather Agency predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Uttarakhand, Telangana, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Lakshadweep for the day. Similar weather conditions are also expected over Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura today.Meanwhile, strong surface winds are expected over Andhra Pradesh till tomorrow.

. Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, Shaktikanta Das has said that restoration of the health of the financial sector has been the defining feature of India’s resilience in recent years. He said, India’s financial sector has emerged as a strong pillar of economic growth, supported by reforms such as the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, bank recapitalization and constructive regulatory oversight. He was speaking at the Kautilya Economic Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today. Mr Das highlighted that the Gross non-performing assets have fallen sharply to 1.68 percent in June this year, while bank profitability has improved significantly. Mr Das said the prudent management of the external sector has also supported India’s efforts towards macroeconomic stability. He also mentioned that India’s external sector indicators have remained broadly resilient due to a mix of factors like the ongoing diversification of exports, conclusion of free trade agreements and sustained surplus in services trade. Mr Das said that the current account deficit for 2025-26 remained well within manageable levels at 0.6 percent of GDP.Secretary in the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Saurabh Garg, today said India’s economic resilience, supported by strong corporate performance and sustained investment activity, is now being reflected in upward revisions to the country’s growth estimates by various international agencies. Talking to the media on the sidelines of the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, Mr. Garg said, the Indian economy had maintained its momentum after recording 7.8 per cent growth in the first quarter of the financial year 2026-27. He noted that strong corporate performance and continued capital investment, including by the private sector, were among the key indicators of the positive economic trend. He added that this momentum was also reflected in recent upward revisions to India’s growth projections by international ratings agencies and research firms, including S&P Global Ratings and Fitch Ratings.On the impact of tensions in West Asia and risks arising from global oil price shocks, Mr. Garg highlighted that government interventions, along with measures taken by households and the private sector, had helped limit the adverse impact of external shocks on the Indian economy.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated the Men’s Cricket Team on retaining their title at the Asian Games 2026. In a series of social media post, Mr Modi said that this is indeed a joyous occasion for the nation. He also wished the team members for their future endeavours.Mr Modi said the 2026 Asian Games have been truly special for Indian Hockey. He congratulated the Men’s Hockey Team on retaining the Asian Games Gold with a commanding victory in the final. He said it has been an exceptional campaign by the players, with back-to-back Asian Games Golds for the first time and a fifth Gold overall. He said the triumph becomes even more special as, for the first time, both Indian Men’s and Women’s Hockey Teams have won Gold at the same Asian Games. He stated that it is clear that Indian Hockey stands tall on the Asian stage.The Prime Minister also congratulated Pranavi Sharath Urs on winning India’s first-ever Gold in Women’s Individual Golf at the Asian Games. Mr Modi said that her superb finish has given the nation a sporting moment to remember. He wished that the victory would draw more young Indians to the game and inspire them to aim for the very top.Mr Modi also congratulated Kumkum Anil Mohod on becoming the first Indian woman to win Recurve Individual Gold at the 2026 Asian Games. He said that her composure in the decisive shoot-off was particularly outstanding. The Prime Minister wished her for future endeavours, and called her to keep aiming higher.Prime Minister also congratulated Aman Sehrawat for scripting history by winning India’s first-ever Asian Games Gold in the Men’s 57kg Freestyle Wrestling event. He added that from Bronze at the last Asian Games to standing atop the podium this time, Aman has displayed great tenacity.Mr Modi expressed happiness that six decades later, India is back on the podium in the Men’s 97kg Freestyle Wrestling event at the Asian Games. He said, Deepak Punia brought home the Bronze after a fiercely contested bout, adding a new chapter to India’s wrestling journey.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is holding bilateral discussions with Swiss President Guy Parmelin in New Delhi.During the talks, they will review progress in bilateral cooperation across a wide range of areas, including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation, mobility, culture, and people-to-people contact. The leaders will also exchange views on regional and global developments, including cooperation in multilateral fora.President Parmelin arrived in New Delhi this morning on a three-day state visit to India, accompanied by a high-level delegation comprising senior officials and business leaders. He was received by Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Ajay Tamta at the airport.The visiting dignitary was accorded a ceremonial welcome at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the Swiss President. He was given a tri-services guard of honour.Talking to reporters after the ceremonial welcome, Mr Parmelin said that the visit is an excellent opportunity to emphasise the importance that both Switzerland and India attach to this relationship.He said, the relationship between the two countries is built on shared democratic values, as well as on trust and mutual respect. Swiss President said that his visit is a stepping stone towards further growth, deepening and strengthening of our close, broad and long-standing partnership.External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today called on President Parmelin. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar appreciated President Parmelin’s sentiments towards deepening the India-Switzerland partnership, building on the promise of India – EFTA TEPA.He expressed confidence that Mr Parmelin’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi will further engagement across a wide range of domains.The visiting dignitary paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. President Parmelin will meet President Droupadi Murmu this evening. President Murmu will also host an official banquet in the honour of her Swiss Counterpart.

. Flydubai flight’s Omani co-pilot tried to crash aircraft in Saudi desert after hijack attempt was foiled, reports Italian newspaper Corriere Della Sera.The paper says, Omani co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami attacked Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar to take control of the plane and crash it into a building at Tel Aviv in Israel.Al-Hammami’s original plot was to kill Flight Captain Smit Machchhar, fly the plane to Tel Aviv, and crash it into one of the city’s skyscrapers, the report claimed, citing Israeli intelligence.According to the newspaper, Hammami realised his original plan could not be carried out, so he decided to crash the plane in the desert.He switched off the autopilot and pushed the control stick. Within 30 seconds, the aircraft lost 16,000 feet of altitude and was on its way to hit the ground.Al-Hammami tried to damage the controls of the aircraft as well before the passengers overpowered him. Yaniv Hayoun, a plumber by profession, pulled the control stick towards him and prevented the plane from losing altitude further.Later, the two off-duty pilots took control of the aircraft. The pilots safely landed the plane. Captain Smit Machchhar was rushed to the hospital, and his co-pilot was handed over to the authorities in Saudi Arabia.Israel has described the incident as a terror attack and is probing how a pilot from Oman — with whom Israel has no diplomatic relations — was cleared to fly into Tel Aviv, flouting its security policy.

The United States has moved all long-range bombers deployed at Britain’s RAF Fairford back to their home stations in the US following an unspecified new threat, citing a US official, amid an ongoing investigation into an alleged Iranian plot targeting the UK airbase.The official did not provide details about the nature of the threat or explain why the aircraft were moved.The relocation comes days after British authorities arrested several individuals in connection with an alleged Iranian plot targeting the airbase where the US aircraft had been stationed.Earlier, British police arrested five men on September 27 on suspicion of terror and explosives offences near RAF Fairford. The men, identified as British nationals aged between 23 and 25 from the London area, were later released on bail.Meanwhile, Iran has denied involvement in the incident and described the accusations as baseless. Tehran also summoned the British ambassador in Tehran following the allegations.

SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk has confirmed that the company’s artificial intelligence arm, SpaceXAI (Artificial Intelligence), will be renamed SpaceXSI (Super Intelligence).The move follows Trump’s executive order titled Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence, signed on September 29, which directs departments and agencies across the US executive branch to use the terms “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official correspondence, public communications, policy documents and non-statutory documents.The order also directs the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology to propose a federal definition of “Super Intelligence” and “SI” reflecting the state of the technology and identify any additional executive action needed to implement the proposed definition.US President Donald Trump has taken decisive action to ensure that the United States leads and wins in Super Intelligence and that all Americans benefit from Super Intelligence and its vast economic benefits.

. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has paid tributes to Guru Nanak Dev on his Jyoti Jyot Day today. In a social media post, Mr Birla said that Guru Nanak Dev imparted lessons of truth, compassion, humanity, and goodness to the world through his life.He added that Guru Nanak Dev fearlessly raised his voice against superstitions, discrimination, caste hierarchies, and social evils prevalent in society.The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that Guru Nanak Dev’s message, based on love, compassion, service, truth, brotherhood, and mutual respect, remains just as relevant today.

The Nifty shed 199 points or 0.9 per cent to settle at 22,422.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 as well as the Smallcap 100 indices tumbled one per cent each.

. In the Asian Games, India won the gold in Men’s cricket, defeating arch-rivals Pakistan in the T20 cricket final at Nisshin, Japan, today. India won the final by 19 runs. Chasing India’s target of 212 runs, Pakistan managed to score only 196 for six in their stipulated 20 overs.Earlier, India posted 211 for six after opting to bat first. Opener Abhishek Sharma scored 61 off 28 balls, while Tilak Varma remained unbeaten on 51 off 22 balls. Shivam Dube added 27 off 14 balls to take India past the 200-run mark. For Pakistan, Hasan Nawaz scored 96 runs while left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas and pacer Ahmed Daniyal took two wickets each.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi has stressed that there is no military or sanctions-based solution to the conflict with the United States, describing diplomacy as the only way to end the hostilities. Speaking to ambassadors and representatives of countries and international organisations in Tehran today, Araghchi expressed hope that the US would pick wisdom and rationality and asserted that Iran is more prepared than before if the US opts for a military course. Araghchi’s remarks came amid continuing tensions surrounding the conflict and mounting economic pressure on Iran.Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump hassaid, thewar with Iran would end very quickly and predicted that oil prices would fall sharply once the conflictwasover. He also portrayed Iran as facing severe military and economic pressure.

. India won five gold, two silver and two bronze medals at the Asian Games in Japan today.In Hockey, India thrashed Malaysia 5-1 to defend their men’s gold and the triumph also secured them a direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. For India, captain Harmanpreet Singh netted two goals while Jugraj, Hardik and Shilanand scored one goal each.In Men’s Cricket, India won the gold defeating arch-rivals Pakistan by 19 runs in the T20 final at Nisshin.Wrestler Aman Sehrawat clinched the men’s 57kg gold after edging out North Korea’s world champion Chong Song Han 11-7 in a fierce final. Kumkum Mohod won the individual gold medal in the women’s recurve archery event.In Golf, Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games gold medal in the women’s individual title. India also bagged silver in the team event.Wrestler Antim Panghal sealed a silver medal in the women’s 53 kg category.Deepak Punia won bronze in the men’s 97kg freestyle wrestling event after defeating Mongolia’s Gankhuyag Ganbaatar.  Archer Neeraj Chauhan got bronze in the men’s individual recurve event.With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fourth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 85, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals.

India and Canada will kick off the fifth round of negotiations for their proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) in Ottawa today, as both sides aim to conclude the trade pact by the end of 2026.The five-day negotiations will continue till 9th of this month. The previous round concluded in New Delhi on 18th of last month, with officials now pushing for faster progress towards a final agreement.In March this year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Canadian counterpart Mark Carney set a year-end target to complete the negotiations for the CEPA between the two countries and agreed to deepen bilateral collaboration in the energy and critical mineral sectors during their meeting in New Delhi.According to the joint statement issued after their summit, the leaders expressed confidence that a comprehensive trade framework would serve as a durable economic anchor for the partnership and support the shared aspiration of expanding bilateral trade to 4.65 lakh crore rupees by 2030.India-Canada bilateral trade in goods stood at 8.66 billion US dollars in 2024-25, while India’s exports to the country touched 4.22 billion US dollars.

The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has emphasised that Russia is a country that stood by India in many ways when India’s security and territorial integrity was under threat.Speaking at the 62nd Munich Security Conference in New Delhi, the External Affairs Minister stressed that at a time when much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to India, Russia was a country with which India’s relations were very good. He said India-Russia relations are shaped by that legacy in many ways.He said the bilateral relationship has widened beyond that today, and it is very much an economic relationship as well. Dr Jaishankar said there are military, nuclear and space components along with a significant amount of trade and investment between the two countries.Dr Jaishankar termed the Russia-Ukraine conflict as unfortunate, saying that India’s position has been very clear that it would like to see an end to this conflict. He expressed New Delhi’s belief that this will require dialogue and diplomacy and there has to be negotiations on this regard.He admitted that India has, in recent months, got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. He added that India had conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard, and is trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has said, international peace and security, supply chain resilience, and connectivity are important agendas for Emerging and Middle Powers, EMPs. Speaking at the 62nd Munich Security Conference in New Delhi today, the External Affairs Minister said, Emerging and Middle Powers are from Global South and Global North, who are united in their goal of being more relevant. He pointed out that the world is changing, its agenda and landscape is changing, and there is a substantial agenda for emerging and middle powers to cooperate.Dr Jaishankar drove home the point that the changing landscape which drives the Emerging and Middle Powers debate is one of a repositioning of the US, the rise of China, and greater interdependence. He highlighted that EMPs’ approach is to de-risk and to diversify, and pursue agenda-based cooperation. He added that the resulting outcome is multipolarity, multi-alignment and small groups. He remarked that the emerging and middle powers have an interest in strengthening their interstate cooperation, but it is also natural that they would have cooperation with the US and China. He cited Quad as an example of emerging middle-power cooperation with an emerging power. He further stated that in the field of connectivity, there is the India-Middle East-Europe Connectivity Corridor, the International North-South Transport Corridor, and the Northern Sea Route. Dr Jaishankar stated that BRICS is an example of various parties who feel that their collective voice is much stronger than the individual ones.Later, in conversation with President of Munich Security Conference, Wolfgang Ischinger, and State Secretary, Germany’s Federal Foreign Office, Bernard Kotsch, Dr Jaishankar said India has decades of high growth ahead and a demography which will sustain that level of growth. He observed that India has historically tended to look at the larger nations of Europe, which is not the case anymore, and India is in the process ofintensifying its relationshipwith the EU. He added that advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, AI and space capabilities are areas where India-EU partnership can increase. The External Affairs Minister also highlighted that many Indian defence start-ups have found partners abroad and defence exports are growing rapidly.

The seven OPEC-plus countries – Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman, have decided to maintain their September 2026 production quotas unchanged for November.The decision was taken during a virtual meeting on October 4, where the countries reviewed global oil market conditions and outlook.  The group will continue to meet monthly, with the next meeting scheduled for November 1.Separately, the 68th meeting of the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (JMMC) stressed the importance of protecting international maritime routes and energy infrastructure, warning that attacks or disruptions could increase market volatility and affect energy supply.
